They have fantastic prices, which is why I go back.  But customer service and shipping delays are where I have an issue.  I receive some orders with no issues at all.  But I have also had numerous instances where:1. I have placed orders, and a label has been created.  But then I have waited 10 days or more for them to ship.  Even though my account says "shipped," the tracking number says USPS doesn't have possession.  It's not shipped if USPS doesn't have it.2. I place an order and the order is unfulfilled for 10-14 days - no label, no updates, etc.In both instances, when I have reached out to customer service, there is suddenly movement.  Either the shipping label is created (once, I received notice of label creation while I was *on the chat*), or the item suddenly shows up at the USPS.And sometimes, they don't even respond to my inquiry.  The item just shows up at the USPS and their system sends me an automated email that the item is on the way.Most recently, I ordered Christmas gifts almost a month before Christmas.  I waited two business weeks for the package to ship.  No notification from the company about any kind of delay.  I sent an inquiry.  Within 24 hours, the package is at the USPS.From their policy: "Orders placed before 1:30 PM Eastern Standard Time on a business day will be processed and shipped out on the same day, provided that the ordered goods are in stock and customer identification is verified."So.  If the delay is caused by an item not being in stock, one of two things should happen 1) you shouldn't be able to place an order for out-of-stock items 2) but if you do, you should be notified that the item is out of stock and that you order is delayed.Otherwise, according to their policy, it should be shipped out the same day.Emails have dates, and so does the USPS tracking system.  Screenshots will clearly show the number of days the order date in my account and my email inquiry.  It will also show the date/time correlation between my inquiry, an email from the company that the item is on the way, and the receipt of the package by the USPS (*actual* shipment).And I can show this not once.  Not twice.  But numerous times.So now I know better than to just let my orders sit.  So my best advice is that if you order from them, just keep your eye on your tracking until you see USPS has your box.  And if it's been significantly past the number of business days stated in their shipping policy, reach out.  Shop.  But be vigilant.While I really appreciate the immediate response when they realize they haven't shipped my item, the bigger concern is whether the item would have shipped at all if I hadn't inquired.This is a respectful *but honest* review.  If the company responds to this post by gaslighting, being retaliatory, or downplaying the issue, here's what I have to say to you, my fellow consumer: "I rest my case."

In my case, I received the 4000USD watch with original box timely, just lack of manufacture's certificate (which has been claimed on jomashop). Bad side in my case (might be just "the Unlikely Event"): when I opened the box and checked watch, one strap detached from the watch suddenly...I was scared...If it happens when wearing it, the watch wound hit the ground.... I had worried about whether Jomashop would set up traps or difficulties for refund... The result proved my worry is not necessary: Once you return the watch without changing its unworn status, refund will be done soon. Especially if you paid it via PAYPAL. As a company running more than 20 year, credibility is "gold".So friends, no need worry about whether Jomashop will cheat you...that is impossible. Have to say: many of them are not fair and kind of subjective. Because service is important to us, and because there are other places where the policies are more customer-friendly, we now shop around rather than defaulting to JS.Would we shop there again? Possibly. We aren't as mad as we were at first and they do have some good products at a great price. But JS is no longer our "go to" site. I will say, though, that the Roee (the person in charge of managing service for a huge volume of sales) makes himself very accessable if a problem occurs. So, if you have a problem, track him down and he should be willing and able to help.At the same time, it would be great if the JS customer support team would ask more clarifying questions before responding to concerns(ie both the response from the CS agents as well as the response to my first post had a number of incorrect assumptions in them). We call ALL up our game a degree or two, and that would be my suggestion for the JS team so they can continue to provide world-class service.
